# technitium_permissions_dns_client (Resource)

Manages who may view, modify and delete in the DnsClient section. The lists set here are the section's full lists: users and groups left out lose their rights. The server always keeps `Administrators` with full rights, whatever is set: leave them out, or list them with full rights. Destroying the resource leaves the permissions as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_group" "perms_dns_client_ops" {
  name = "Ops dns_client"
}

# Groups the server keeps with full rights need not be listed.
resource "technitium_permissions_dns_client" "this" {
  group_permissions = [
    { name = technitium_group.perms_dns_client_ops.name, can_view = true, can_modify = false, can_delete = false },
  ]

  # Deleting or replacing the group makes the server delete its rights.
  # This sets them again in the same apply.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [technitium_group.perms_dns_client_ops]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `group_permissions` (Attributes Set) The rights of groups. The server always keeps `Administrators` with full rights, whatever is set: leave them out, or list them with full rights. Leaving it out keeps the server's. The server silently drops a group that does not exist, and apply fails: refer to the `technitium_group` resource, or add `depends_on`, so the group is created first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--group_permissions))
- `user_permissions` (Attributes Set) The rights of individual users. An empty set removes them; leaving it out keeps the server's. The server silently drops a user that does not exist, and apply fails: refer to the `technitium_user` resource, or add `depends_on`, so the user is created first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--user_permissions))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.

- `can_delete` (Boolean) May delete in the section.
- `can_modify` (Boolean) May change the section.
- `can_view` (Boolean) May view the section.
- `name` (String) The group name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import technitium_permissions_dns_client.this permissions_dns_client
```
